key_insight: Small-radius, high-electronegativity A-site dopants like Ca can improve both proton transport and chemical stability in BaCeO3-based perovskite electrolytes by weakening A–O bonding and shrinking the lattice.
engineering_relevance: A-site doping offers a practical design lever for proton-conducting SOFC electrolytes, potentially reducing degradation from CO2/SO2 while preserving or improving conductivity.
method: Mechanistic analysis of A-site dopant effects on vacancy formation, proton uptake, and adsorption
Comparison of how ionic radius and electronegativity influence transport and stability
evidence_signal: The abstract reports computational evidence that Ca doping lowers A–O bond strength, facilitates oxygen-vacancy formation and proton uptake, and reduces adsorption strength for acidic gases, supporting the proposed dual improvement.
watch_item: Benefits may depend on proton-transfer-limited conditions, and Ca surface segregation/grain-boundary effects could complicate real-device performance.
paper_title: Role of small-radius and high-electronegativity A-Site dopants in enhancing proton transport and stability of perovskite electrolytes
